card.name: Warning statements: is contraindicated, not approved
card.fires_on: Short linking or closing marks inside warning text, such as 'is' or 'are' after a drug name before 'contraindicated' or 'not approved', and the colon after CAUTION or the period ending a risk sentence.

modes.label: Verb after drug name
modes.description: 'is' or 'are' right after a product name, leading into a contraindication or not-approved statement.
modes.example: IZERVAY<< is>> contraindicated in patients with oc

modes.label: End of warning clause
modes.description: A colon or period closing a caution or a serious-risk sentence.
modes.example: respiratory depression, coma, and death<<.>> Reserve concomitant prescribing of Methad

modes.label: Boxed warning openers
modes.description: A word in a short imperative warning, such as 'this' after Keep.
modes.example: Keep<< this>> product out of the reach of children.

card.writes: Little clear effect; it suppresses exclamation marks, which fits the flat tone of warning text.
card.plain: It fires at the small joining words and punctuation in stern warning statements, especially just before 'contraindicated'.
